courses.subject: PHILOS
courses.title: Philosophical Topics in Feminist Theory
courses.description: An analytical study of selected philosophical issues arising out of feminist theory, such as the nature of autonomy, or the relation between gender and knowledge. Prereq: 6 cr hrs in Philos at or above 2000-level; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs or 2 completions.
courses.prereq: 6 cr hrs in Philos at or above 2000-level; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHILOS
courses.title: Advanced Symbolic Logic
courses.description:
Introduction to the metatheory of first-order logics and languages; axiomatic development of propositional and predicate logic; model theory; soundness, completeness, and Lowenheim-Skolem theorems.
Prereq: 2500.

courses.subject: PHILOS
courses.title: Advanced Theory of Knowledge
courses.description: An intensive examination of major epistemological problems: the possibility, origin, foundation, structure, methods, limits, types, and validity of knowledge. Preferable to have credit for 3750 prior to enrollment. Prereq: 2500, and 6 cr hrs in Philos at or above 3000-level; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 660.
courses.prereq: 2500, and 6 cr hrs in Philos at or above 3000-level; or Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHILOS
courses.title: Advanced Philosophy of Mind
courses.description:
Classical and contemporary approaches to the nature of mind, mind-body, other minds, intentionality, and other problems. Preferable to have credit for 3800 prior to enrollment.
Prereq: 6 cr hrs in Philos at or above 3000-level; or Grad standing in Philos; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 6 cr hrs in Philos at or above 3000-level; or Grad standing in Philos; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: World of Energy: Light, Thermodynamics, Energy Sources
courses.description: An examination of the various forms of energy and energy production with its personal and global impact.  Uses the hands-on discovery mode of instruction. Intended for non-science majors.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 104.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 104

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Physics by Inquiry: Properties of Matter, Heat and Temperature, and Forces and Motion
courses.description:
Investigation of the properties of matter, motion and thermodynamics using the inquiry technique.  Intended for non-science majors.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for Physics 106 and 107.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for Physics 106 and 107

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: The Physics of Sports
courses.description:
Students learn how to apply fundamental concepts of physics to sports. They collect data of sports actions and construct physics models to represent, calculate, analyze, interpret, and explain the motion and interactions between people and equipment. Students learn how to make useful and appropriate approximations in these complex environments. This is a GE Foundations Natural Sciences course.
Prereq: Math 1050 or equiv. Not open to students with credit for 1110.
courses.prereq: Math 1050 or equiv

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Practicing Physics - Matter, Heat, and Motion
courses.description:
Students work in groups to perform hands-on investigations on density, motion, and thermodynamics and develop models to describe and explain their observations. Through discussions with instructors and peers, students consider the effects of science in society and apply their scientific skills to everyday situations. Intended for non-science majors, especially those contemplating a teaching career. 
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1106.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1106

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Mechanics, Kinematics, Fluids, Waves
courses.description:
Algebra-based introduction to classical physics: Newtons laws, fluids, waves.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in Math 1120 or 1148, or Math Placement Level M.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in Math 1120 or 1148, or Math Placement Level M

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: E&M, Optics, Modern Physics
courses.description:
Algebra-based introduction to electricity and magnetism, simple optics, overview of modern physics including special relativity and quantum mechanics.
Prereq: 1200, 1249, 1250, 1260, or 1270.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Mechanics, Work, and Energy
courses.description:
PHYSICS 1248 is the first course in a two-course series, for students in physical sciences, mathematics, and engineering. This course covers rotational dynamics, fluids, thermal dynamics, and vibrational motion. The physics content in relation to these topics is covered in the same depth and rigor as in PHYSICS 1250. The combination of PHYSICS 1248 + PHYSICS 1249 is equivalent to PHYSICS 1250.
Concur: Math 1120, 1140, 1148, 1149, or 1150 or higher; or Math Placement Level M. Not open to students with credit for 1250.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Rotational Dynamics, Thermal Physics, and Vibrational Motion
courses.description:
PHYSICS 1249 is the second course in a two-course series, for students in physical sciences, mathematics, and engineering. This course covers rotational dynamics, fluids, thermal dynamics, and vibrational motion. The physics content in relation to these topics is covered in the same depth and rigor as in PHYSICS 1250. The combination of PHYSICS 1248 + PHYSICS 1249 is equivalent to PHYSICS 1250.
Prereq: 1248. Concur: Math 1121, 1140, 1141, 1149, 1150, or above. Not open to students with credit for 1250.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Mechanics, Work and Energy, Thermal Physics
courses.description:
Calculus-based introduction to classical physics: Newton's laws, work and energy, fluids, thermodynamics; for students in physical sciences, mathematics, and engineering.
Prereq or concur: Math 1141, 1151, 1154, 1156, 1161, 1181H, or 4181H.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Honors Physics: Mechanics and Conservation Laws; Special Relativity
courses.description:
In depth study of classical mechanics including Newton's laws, conservation laws, and  introduction to special relativity.
Prereq: Honors standing, or permission of instructor. Concur: Math 1151 (152), 1161 (161), 1181H (161H), or 4181H (191H) or above. Not open to students with credit for 131.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: E&M, Waves, Optics, Modern Physics
courses.description:
Calculus-based introduction to electricity and magnetism, waves, simple optics, and quantum mechanics; for students in physical sciences, mathematics, engineering.
Prereq: 1248 and 1249, or 1250, 1250H, 1260, or 1270; and Math 1141, 1151, 1154, or above; and Concur: Math 1152, 1155, 1161, 1172, 1181H, or 4181H; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: 1248 and 1249, or 1250, 1250H, 1260, or 1270; and Math 1141, 1151, 1154, or above; and Concur: Math 1152, 1155, 1161, 1172, 1181H, or 4181H; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Honors Physics: Electricity and Magnetism; Thermal Physics, Waves, and Quantum Physics
courses.description:
In depth introduction to: electricity and magnetism including Maxwell's equations, thermodynamics, quantum mechanics.
Prereq: 1250H; or Honors standing and 1250 or 1270; or permission of instructor. Concur: Math 1152, 1161, 1172, 1181H, or 4181H or above.
courses.prereq: 1250H; or Honors standing and 1250 or 1270; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: FEH Physics: Mechanics, Thermal Physics, Waves
courses.description:
Calculus-based introduction to classical physics: Newton's laws, fluids, thermodynamics, waves. Emphasizes group work; for students in Fundamentals of Engineering Honors.
Prereq: Honors standing in Engineering, and 1 entrance unit of Physics or Chem. Concur: Math 1151 (152), 1161 (161), 1181H (161H), or 4181H (191H), or above. Not open to students with credit for 131.
courses.prereq: Honors standing in Engineering, and 1 entrance unit of Physics or Chem

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: FEH Physics: E&M, Optics, Modern Physics
courses.description: Calculus-based introduction to electricity and magnetism, simple optics, modern physics including special relativity and quantum mechanics. courses.prereq: 1260 (131) and Math 1151 (152) or above, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: E&M, Thermal Physics, Waves, and  Quantum Physics for Majors
courses.description:
Calculus-based introduction to classical physics. In depth study of electromagnetism, waves, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics. For students majoring in Astronomy & Astrophysics, Engineering Physics, or Physics.
Prereq:
Option 1: Physics 1270. Prereq or concur: Math 1152, 1155, 1161, 1172, 1181H, or 4181H; Or
Option 2: Physics 1250, 1250H, or 1260. Prereq or concur: Math 1152, 1155, 1161, 1172, 1181H, or 4181H; and enrollment as Astronomy & Astrophysics major, Engineering Physics major or pre-major, or Physics major.
courses.prereq: Option 1: Physics 1270

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Polaris Mentoring Program I
courses.description:
The Polaris Mentorship Class will teach students about issues surrounding the culture of STEM, provide time to meet with a near-peer mentor, and build community and a toolkit of soft skills to succeed in physics and astronomy at OSU.
Prereq: Enrollment in Astronomy & Astrophysics major, Engineering Physics major, Physics major, or University Exploration program; or permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 3 cr hrs. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Enrollment in Astronomy & Astrophysics major, Engineering Physics major, Physics major, or University Exploration program; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Polaris Mentoring Program II
courses.description:
The Polaris Mentorship Class will teach students about issues surrounding diversity and inclusion in STEM, provide time to meet with a near-peer mentor, and introduce students to Physics/Astronomy research at OSU. This is the second and last course of the program.
Prereq: 2050.01, or permission of instructor. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: 2050.01, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Individual Studies
courses.description: Designed to give a properly qualified student opportunity for independent reading, study, or laboratory work in a specialized field of interest. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 20 cr hrs or 5 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Intermediate Mechanics I
courses.description:
Vectors and kinematics; foundations of Newtonian mechanics; momentum, work, and energy; conservative and nonconservative forces; potentials; angular momentum; rotation about a fixed axis; rigid body motion; noninertial systems and fictitious forces.
Prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 1251, 1251H, 1261, or 1271. Concur: Math 2153, 2162.01, 2162.02, 2173, 2182H, or 4182H.
courses.prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 1251, 1251H, 1261, or 1271

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Intermediate Mechanics II
courses.description: The special theory of relativity; relativistic kinematics; relativistic momentum and energy.  Introduction to quantum systems; photons; the Bohr atom; matter waves. Prereq: Math 2153 or 2173 (254) or above, and a grade of C+ or above in 2300 (261). Not open to students with credit for 262 or 263.
courses.prereq: Math 2153 or 2173 (254) or above, and a grade of C+ or above in 2300 (261)

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Physics
courses.description: Undergraduate research or creative activities in various topics. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 20 cr hrs or 4 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Experimental Physics Instrumentation and Data Analysis Lab
courses.description:
Construction, simulation and statistical analysis of data from advanced experiments in nuclear processes. Introduction to advanced instrumentation and computer controlled data acquisition. Computer programming is required.
Prereq: 1251, 1251H, 1261, or 1271; and CSE 1222, 1223, 1224, Engr 1221, Engr 1281H, or Astron 1221.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Individual Studies
courses.description: Designed to give a properly qualified student opportunity for independent reading, study, or laboratory work in a specialized field of interest. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 3 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Introductory Electronics for Physicists
courses.description:
Intermediate level introduction to electronic circuits, devices, and instrumentation with emphasis on laboratory experience.
Prereq: 1251, 1251H, 1261, or 1271.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Physics
courses.description: Undergraduate research or creative activities in various topics. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 3 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Honors Undergraduate Research in Physics
courses.description: Undergraduate research or creative activities in various topics; no thesis. Prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 3 completions.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Thesis Undergraduate Research in Physics
courses.description: Undergraduate research or creative activities in various topics; culminating in a thesis. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 3 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Honors Thesis Undergraduate Research in Physics
courses.description:
Undergraduate research or creative activities in various topics; culminating in a thesis.
Prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 3 completions.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Theoretical Mechanics
courses.description:
Development of Lagrangian mechanics, inertia and stress tensors, rigid body rotations and introduction to the mechanics of continuous media. 
Prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 2301; and Math 2415, 2255, 2174, or 5520H.
courses.prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 2301; and Math 2415, 2255, 2174, or 5520H

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Introduction to quantum mechanics, including its historical background, the Schrodinger equation, solutions of one-dimensional scattering and bound state problems. Prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 2301 (263), and Math 2174, 2415 (415), 2255 (255) or 5520H (521H); or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5500H, 631, or 632.
courses.prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 2301 (263), and Math 2174, 2415 (415), 2255 (255) or 5520H (521H); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Honors Quantum Mechanics I
courses.description:
Advanced treatment of quantum mechanics, including its historical background, the Schrodinger equation, solutions of one-dimensional scattering and bound state problems. Uses Dirac notation.
Prereq: Honors status, a grade of B or above in 2301, and a grade of B- or above in Math 2174, 2415, 2255 or 5520H; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5500.
courses.prereq: Honors status, a grade of B or above in 2301, and a grade of B- or above in Math 2174, 2415, 2255 or 5520H; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description:
Harmonic oscillator, time-independent and time-dependent perturbation theory, addition of angular momenta, fine and hyperfine structure of hydrogen, identical particles, periodic systems, modern physics applications of quantum mechanics.
Prereq: 5500, and Math 2174, 2415, 2255, or 5520H; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5501H or 633.
courses.prereq: 5500, and Math 2174, 2415, 2255, or 5520H; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Honors Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description:
The Schrodinger equation in three dimensions, angular momentum, the hydrogen atom; time-independent perturbation theory, time-dependent perturbation theory, scattering theory and the Born approximation, multi-electron atoms.
Prereq: A grade of B- or above in 5500H; or Honors standing and a grade of B+ or above in 5500; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 5501.
courses.prereq: A grade of B- or above in 5500H; or Honors standing and a grade of B+ or above in 5500; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Big Data Analytics in Physics
courses.description:
Provides an introduction to machine learning and advanced algorithms, with an emphasis on practical physics-based applications, using publicly available data sets. The goal is to provide an introduction to Data Science for students who may want to pursue this as a career option and/or apply these techniques in a research environment.
Prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 1251, 1251H, 1261, or 1271; and CSE 1222, 1223, 1224, Engr 1221, 1281H, or Astron 1221; and enrollment in Physics, Engineering Physics, or Astronomy major; or permission of instructor.
courses.prereq: A grade of C+ or above in 1251, 1251H, 1261, or 1271; and CSE 1222, 1223, 1224, Engr 1221, 1281H, or Astron 1221; and enrollment in Physics, Engineering Physics, or Astronomy major; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Advanced Physics Laboratory
courses.description: Lab course for physics majors. Three advanced experiments from a variety of physics disciplines are carried out. Emphasis is on experimental techniques, analysis of collected data, and formal presentation of experimental results. Prereq: 2301 (263); and 3700 (416); and 5400 (555) or 5400H; and 5500 (631) or 5500H. Not open to students with credit for 616.

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Engineering Physics Design I
courses.description:
Presents fundamentals of engineering-physics design and leads to skills development relevant to a specific design proposal. Technical communication skills, both written and oral, are employed throughout.
Prereq: 2301; and Sr standing in Engineering Physics.
courses.prereq: 2301; and Sr standing in Engineering Physics

courses.subject: PHYSICS
courses.title: Engineering Physics Design II
courses.description: Continues training in engineering-physics design. Preliminary designs are refined and prototypes are fabricated and tested. Technical communication skills, both written and oral, are employed throughout. Prereq: 5800, and Sr standing in Engineering Physics.
courses.prereq: 5800, and Sr standing in Engineering Physics

courses.subject: POLISH
courses.title: Advanced Polish I
courses.description: Further develop speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills and grammar competence. Prereq: 2104. Not open to students with credit for Slavic 5194 (Au13, Cretu).
courses.department: Slavic and East European Languages and Cultures

courses.subject: POLISH
courses.title: Advanced Polish II
courses.description: Further develop speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills and grammar competence. Prereq: 3101. Not open to students with credit for Slavic 5194 (Sp15, Advanced Polish).
courses.department: Slavic and East European Languages and Cultures

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to American Politics
courses.description:
Introduction to American politics, the institutions and processes which create public policy, the strengths and weaknesses of the American political systems.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 3100 (300), 101, or 101H.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 3100 (300), 101, or 101H

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to American Politics and Civics
courses.description:
This course provides a comprehensive overview of the institutions, processes, and behaviors that shape American government. By exploring general concepts regarding American government institutions and political behavior, you will not only learn the "rules of the game", three branches of government but also understand how the American people engage in the politics, and the complex dynamics between the government and the public.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1100, 1165, 1166.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1100, 1165, 1166

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to Civics and Politics
courses.description:
Explores ways citizens can interact with the political systems that govern them through examination of seminal texts and discussions about the nature of the economic and social institutions that drive the economy, structure our free market competition, and define our particular form of capitalism.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1165.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1165

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
courses.description:
Introduction to modern nation-states outside the United States: problems of state- and nation-building, representation, conflict, and making of government policy in selected countries.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 100 or 100H.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 100 or 100H

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Global Politics
courses.description:
Cooperation and conflict in world politics. Covers basic theories of international relations and key issues, including security, political economy, international organizations, and the environment.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 145 or 145H.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 145 or 145H

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to the Politics of Identity
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the continued significance of race, gender, and ethnicity in American society with a focus on identity. Examines how various identities and combinations of identities (namely race, ethnicity, and gender) are associated with sociopolitical experiences and attitudes.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: American Government Culture and Behavior
courses.description: Focuses on political elites, theories of American Democracy, development of institutions, and importance of mass political behavior and organized interests.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Follow the Science: The Politics of Health
courses.description: In the 20th Century, chronic conditions became the leading killers of Americans and the federal government came to play a much more expansive role in health, including the approval of treatments, regulation of harmful substances, promotion of healthy habits, and funding healthcare. Students will survey these developments and apply the resulting insights to contemporary health policy debates.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Voters and Elections
courses.description: Students will engage in an in-depth study of the mechanics of democracy. Students will take a close look at various forms of voting and representation around the world and examine the motivation and tactics of elite actors (candidates, reporters, interest groups, political parties, media personalities, etc.) and the voting public.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: American Foreign Policy
courses.description:
The role of the United States in world politics since the Second World War, emphasizing structural change in economic and political-military relations.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 245 or 245H.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 245 or 245H

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in American Politics
courses.description:
Discussion of and critical writing about controversies in contemporary American politics; aimed at fostering analytical abilities in reading comprehension, oral, and written expression.
Prereq: 101 or 300, and English 110 or 111, and Soph standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 367.01 or 367.01H.
courses.prereq: 101 or 300, and English 110 or 111, and Soph standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to Political Theory
courses.description:
An introduction to the field of political theory through classic and contemporary texts and selected case studies.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 210 or 210H.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 210 or 210H

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Introduction to the Policy Process
courses.description: Introduction to the workings of policy-making processes within governments, and the use of social science reasoning to evaluate and improve the content of policies.   Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 305.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 305

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Political Psychology
courses.description: Introduces students to political psychology, its development from parent disciplines, its topics and problems, its research results and methods, and their applications to current affairs. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 403 or Psych 403.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 403 or Psych 403

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Political Science Internship
courses.description: Combines experience in political institutions or policy processes with analysis of that experience.  Prereq: Permission of the department. Repeatable to a maximum of 4 cr hrs.  This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of the department

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Politics of the Developing World
courses.description:
A general introduction to the theoretical and substantive literature dealing with the historical development and contemporary characteristics of the new states of Asia and Africa.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 541.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 541

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Political Violence
courses.description: This course will expose students to major theoretical debates and broad empirical patterns of intrastate conflict during the post-World War II era.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Politics of Sports
courses.description: Introduces students to the interactions between politics and the world of sports.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Politics of Markets
courses.description:
Introduction to the interaction between politics and markets, in theory and in practice. We study how markets are embedded in political and social institutions, and how political systems and markets are organized across time and space.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4280.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4280

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Comparative Public Policy
courses.description: This course serves as an introduction to public policy in comparative perspective; its focus is on wealthy democracies. The first part of the course explores broad theories about how and why public policy differs so dramatically across countries. The second part of the course focuses on cross-national differences across specific policy domains.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Political Analysis of International Economic Relations
courses.description:
Examines the relationship between political and economic events in the international system; topics include global interdependence, inequality, scarce resources, and periphery nation strategies.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4380.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4380

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Global Justice
courses.description: Examines the idea of justice between states and among the people of the world. What would a just world look like? How should we live in our unjust world? Current debates about war, the environment, diversity and poverty will be considered.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Survey Research in Political Science
courses.description: The conducting of public opinion polls. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 449, 581, or Comm 449.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 449, 581, or Comm 449

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Data Literacy and Data Visualization
courses.description: Introduction to the tools of data analysis in political science, with an emphasis on data visualization.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Identity Politics
courses.description: Explores who controls the meaning of identity in society; examining identity from the perspective of liberal, sociological, and social psychological, structuralist, and institutionalist theories.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 547.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 547

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Political Leadership
courses.description: Establishment of a working definition of political leadership, investigation of recruitment of leaders, analysis of major functions political leaders perform, and assessment of consequences of political leadership.  Prereq: 1100 (100), 1200 (101), or 3100 (300).  Not open to students with credit for 612.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Careers in Political Science
courses.description: Designed to help students explore different career paths related to Political Science, engage with professionals working within a range of careers, and build a portfolio in preparation for entering the job market

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: U.S. Congress
courses.description:
Analysis of legislatures and legislators, with a focus on the U.S. Congress and some attention to state legislatures and representative assemblies in other countries.  
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 517.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 517

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Governing Urban America
courses.description:
This course will examine the major problems facing urban communities in the 21st Century; the economic, social, and political forces that have historically shaped - and continue to influence - their development; the role of government in addressing urban problems; and the major participants and stakeholders in city politics.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 505.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 505

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Law and Politics
courses.description: Analysis of the roles of judges and lawyers as participants in the American political process; analysis of courts as political institutions.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 516.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 516

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: American Supreme Court
courses.description: This course focuses on the U.S. Supreme Court as an institution and emphasizes the ways in which its formal and informal norms and structures shape the nature and content of the law the Court makes.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Supreme Court Decision Making
courses.description: Study of explanations for Supreme Court decisions; use of those explanations and independent research to predict justices' positions in current cases.  Prereq: Honors standing or permission of instructor.  Not open to students with credit for 521H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing or permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: American Constitutional Law
courses.description: Assessment of the contemporary realities of U.S. governmental authority as interpreted by the judiciary; emphasis on judicial review, case and controversy requirements, and legislative and executive power.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 520.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 520

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: American Constitutional Law
courses.description:
Assessment of the contemporary realities of U.S. governmental authority as interpreted by the judiciary; emphasis on judicial review, case and controversy requirements, and legislative and executive power. 
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4135.
.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4135

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Civil Liberties
courses.description: An examination of civil liberties decisions by American courts, their legal and political bases, and their effects on government and society.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 519.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 519

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Women and the Law
courses.description: An examination of the legal status of women and the ways in which law affects the situation of women in American society.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 514.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 514

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Gun Politics
courses.description: Examination of the arguments and issues surrounding gun control in the United States. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 518.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 518

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Gun Politics
courses.description:
Examination of the arguments and issues surrounding gun control in the United States.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4139 (518).
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4139 (518)

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Black Politics
courses.description: Economic, political, and social constraints on the development of black political power; the efforts made by black people in recent times to organize for effective political action. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 504 or AfAmASt 4504 (504). Cross-listed in AfAmASt 4504.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 504 or AfAmASt 4504 (504)

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Campaign Politics
courses.description: The organization and strategy of American political campaigns; practical politics seen in the light of knowledge about political behavior and public opinion.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 502.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 502

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Public Opinion
courses.description: Origins and nature of political attitudes; the content of public opinion; the public's influence on policy-making.  Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 503.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 503

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Media and American Politics
courses.description:
This course presents the modern study of the media and it role in the American political system, including supply and demand pressures and how they affect media content, its effects on citizens, and the emerging role of social media in politics.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 509.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 509

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Combines experience in political institutions or policy processes with analysis of that experience in light of relevant scholarly literature.  Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 10 cr hrs or 3 completions.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Policy Analysis
courses.description:
An analysis of the policy process emphasizing the determinants of public policy, theories of public choice, and the implementation, impact, and evaluation of policy decisions.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 679.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 679

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: China: State and Society
courses.description: The 21st-century rise of China and its effects on Chinese politics and society. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 536.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 536

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Domestic Politics of International Conflict
courses.description: Examination of war and the impact of domestic politics on the war-making decision; influence of domestic institutions and public opinion on leaders' ability/willingness to wage war. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 579.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 579

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: African Politics
courses.description: An introductory survey of Sub-Saharan African politics from the pre-colonial period to the contemporary era. It will examine the common themes, issues, and trends that shape politics and development across forty-nine countries. Students will gain an understanding of how context shapes political behavior and how historical and political forces have influenced African politics. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4597.02 (Au13, African Politics), 4250H, or AfAmASt 4250. Cross-listed in AfAmASt.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4597.02 (Au13, African Politics), 4250H, or AfAmASt 4250

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Theories of International Relations
courses.description: Various theories of world politics, such as realism, liberalism, long cycles, domestic and bureaucratic politics, and decision-making level theory. Prereq: 1300 (145).  Not open to students with credit for 550.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Security Policy
courses.description: National security and military policy issues and trends since 1945; covers containment, deterrence, Vietnam, nuclear weapons, terrorism, and globalization. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 552.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 552

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: International Security and the Causes of War
courses.description: Examines various issues regarding international conflict and cooperation, including theories of strategic interaction and the causes of war. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 544.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 544

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: The Politics of International Terrorism
courses.description: Examines international terrorism's concepts and actors, the motivations and causes of terrorism, the experience of the United States, and tensions between freedoms and security. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 548.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 548

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Strategies for War and Peace
courses.description: Introduces critical perspectives on the study of `war? and `peace? in International Relations; special interest in how themes of knowledge production, race, gender, and colonialism intersect with and shape our understandings of war and peace.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Honors Psychology of War and Peace
courses.description:
Examines how states pursue a range of security goals in international politics and why states sometimes succeed but other times fail to cooperate.
Prereq: Honors standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 4322.
courses.prereq: Honors standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Politics in the Middle East
courses.description: Politics of Arab-Israeli relations, Persian Gulf, Islamic fundamentalism, and oil; processes of change and their effects on governments and international relations. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 546.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 546

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Global Governance
courses.description: Examination of emergence and form of global governance, including questions of legitimation, democratization, and enforcement; as well as collective security, humanitarian intervention, and proliferation. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 556.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 556

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: The United Nations System
courses.description: Activities and potential of the United Nations system in promoting economic well-being, environmental management, resource sharing, social justice, and control of violence. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 551.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 551

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Debating Democracy
courses.description: Intensive examination of theories of democracy, focusing on normative and descriptive dilemmas such as participation versus liberty in democratic societies. Prereq: Honors standing or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 565H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing or permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Feminist Political Theory
courses.description: Examines concepts in feminist political theory including the articulation of feminism, the subjects of feminist theory, the relation of race, class and sexuality to gender experience, and the use of feminist theory to transform conceptions of justice. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for WGSSt 4465. Cross-listed in WGSSt.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for WGSSt 4465

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Game Theory for Political Scientists
courses.description: Provides entry-level understanding of the basic concepts of game theory and how these concepts are applied to the study of political phenomena. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4553 (587).
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4553 (587)

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Thesis Research Colloquium
courses.description: Designed for Political Science majors writing senior theses. We will study the elements of a successful research paper including how to formulate a question, how to identify the right method for investigating it, and how to conduct research. Concur: Second semester Jr standing, or permission of instructor.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Data Analysis in Political Science I
courses.description:
Covers basic techniques for analyzing data in political science.
Prereq: Math 1151 and one course in PolitSc at the 3000 level or above; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 485, 4781H (485H), 585, or 585H.
courses.prereq: Math 1151 and one course in PolitSc at the 3000 level or above; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Data Analysis in Political Science II
courses.description: Covers advanced techniques for analyzing data in political science. Prereq: Math 1151 and 4781 (485), or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 586.
courses.prereq: Math 1151 and 4781 (485), or permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Topics in American Politics
courses.description: Selected topics in American politics; topics vary by section and instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 6 cr hrs.

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Business-Government Relations
courses.description: Explores the relationships between business and government, including topics ranging from regulatory politics and legislative lobbying, to trade politics and multinational corporations, to business ethics. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 511.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 511

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Political Science
courses.description: Undergraduate research in variable topics. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 10 cr hrs or 10 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Undergraduate Thesis Research
courses.description: Thesis research with thesis adviser. Minimum of two semesters required of candidates for BA with research distinction in political science. Must meet standards for graduation with research distinction. Prereq: Sr standing, and enrollment in PolitSc major, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 4 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Sr standing, and enrollment in PolitSc major, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research
courses.description: Honors thesis research with thesis adviser. Minimum of two semesters required of candidates for BA with distinction in political science. Prereq: Honors standing, and Sr standing, and enrollment in Political Science major, and permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 4 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and Sr standing, and enrollment in Political Science major, and permission of instructor

courses.subject: POLITSC
courses.title: Life, Liberty, and Property: Early Modern Political Thought
courses.description:
Why do we have government? What are the proper limits of its authority? What should we do when its demands conflict with our moral or religious beliefs? These questions lie at the center of early modern political thought, and gave rise to the idea of the social contract.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4412 (471) or 6412 (671).
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 4412 (471) or 6412 (671)

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Portuguese I
courses.description:
Development of listening, reading, speaking, and writing skills in cultural contexts. Available in classroom-based and 100% online formats. Not open to native speakers of this language through regular course enrollment or EM credit.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1102.01 or 1103.01 or equiv.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 1102.01 or 1103.01 or equiv

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Portuguese II
courses.description:
Development of listening, reading, speaking, and writing skills in cultural contexts. Both classroom-based and 100% online sections available each semester. Not open to native speakers of this language through regular course enrollment or EM credit.
Prereq: 1101.01 or 1101.51. Not open to students with credit for 1102.51 or 5501.

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Portuguese III
courses.description:
Continued development of listening, reading, speaking, and writing skills in cultural contexts. Both classroom-based and 100% online sections available. Not open to native speakers of this language through regular course enrollment or EM credit.
Prereq: 1102.01. Not open to students with credit for 5501 or 5502.

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Introduction to Brazilian Culture
courses.description:
Integrated, multidisciplinary overview of modern Brazilian culture in terms of its visual, plastic, musical, literary, dramatic, and popular arts within socio-economic and political context.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for Portgese 330.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for Portgese 330

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: THE EMPIRE SINGS BACK: Portugal's New African Rhythms & Cultural Resistance in the European Diaspora
courses.description: Exploration of the vibrant African & Afro-Portuguese musical genres that have emerged in Portugal as a result of a longstanding colonial and imperial history connecting Portugal and several African continent countries. Focus on how race, ethnicity, & gender interact with music production, fruition, and distribution. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Internship & Career Exploration
courses.description:
Internship for academic credit under employer supervision, with enrollment and grade evaluation by a faculty sponsor and program coordinator in the Dept. of Spanish & Portuguese. Student must obtain the internship and submit signed employer and department agreement prior to the start of the internship term. Enrollment in another academic department or college level internship course is not permitted during the same term. This course does not apply to the Portuguese Major or Minor program.
Prereq: 1103, or 5502, or Portuguese Seal of Biliteracy, and GPA of 2.50 or above, and Soph, Jr, or Sr standing; and permission of department. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 4 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: 1103, or 5502, or Portuguese Seal of Biliteracy, and GPA of 2.50 or above, and Soph, Jr, or Sr standing; and permission of department

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Portuguese Conversation and Composition
courses.description: Intensive practice in conversation and composition based on short stories written by Lusophone authors with review of grammar. Not open to native speakers of this language through regular course enrollment or EM credit. Prereq: Portgse 1103.01 (Portgese 103.01 and 104.01) or 5502 (502), or equiv, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for Portgese 202 or 403.
courses.prereq: Portgse 1103.01 (Portgese 103.01 and 104.01) or 5502 (502), or equiv, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Individual Studies
courses.description: Individual studies. Prereq: Portgese 3401 (Portgse 401), 3402 (402), 3403 (403); or 5502 (502) and Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 59 cr hrs or 16 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Portgese 3401 (Portgse 401), 3402 (402), 3403 (403); or 5502 (502) and Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Portuguese Translation
courses.description: Advanced practice in Portuguese-to-English translation based primarily on the contemporary written Portuguese of Brazil and Portugal; emphasis on formal grammar and style. Prereq: Portgse 3401 (Portgese 401), or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for Portgese 510.
courses.prereq: Portgse 3401 (Portgese 401), or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Internship in Portuguese
courses.description:
Use of advanced Lusophone linguistic & cultural skills in a professional training context or industry for academic credit under employer supervision, with enrollment and grade evaluation by a faculty sponsor and program coordinator in the Dept. of Spanish & Portuguese. Student must obtain an internship and submit signed employer and department agreement prior to the start of the internship term. Submission of a completed Internship Enrollment Application & Supervisor Agreement is required. Graduate students must obtain faculty advisor approval and confirm work hour commitment and duties each week of the internship term for enrollment in the appropriate number of credit hours. A maximum of 3 cr may be applied to the undergraduate major or minor program with Undergraduate Studies Committee approval.
Prereq: 3450, and GPA of 2.50 or above, and Soph, Jr, or Sr standing, and permission of department. Repeatable to a maximum of 12 cr hrs or 4 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: 3450, and GPA of 2.50 or above, and Soph, Jr, or Sr standing, and permission of department

courses.subject: PORTGSE
courses.title: Studies in Literatures and Cultures of the Portuguese-Speaking World
courses.description:
Intensive exploration of a specific topic or problem; topic varies, for example: modern Brazilian novel, Luso-African literature, Portuguese poetry since 1974.
Prereq: 3450 (P450) and one 4500 (500) level literature and/or culture course; or 5502 (502) and Grad standing; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 650. Repeatable to a maximum of 9 cr hrs.
courses.prereq: 3450 (P450) and one 4500 (500) level literature and/or culture course; or 5502 (502) and Grad standing; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description:
A prerequisite to advanced courses; a broad survey of psychological science. Application of the scientific method to the empirical study of behavior with emphasis on individual and cultural differences.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 100, 1100H (100H) or 1100E (100E).
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 100, 1100H (100H) or 1100E (100E)

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description:
A prerequisite to advanced courses; a broad survey of psychological science. Application of the scientific method to the empirical study of behavior with emphasis on individual and cultural differences.
Prereq: Honors standing, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 1100 (100), 1100E (100E), or 100H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: I am. The Psychology of Identity and Culture
courses.description: Contemporary and historical research into psychological identity; The science of how individual people experience personal and cultural differences. Reading and discourse on the psychology research of: personality, social roles, cultural neuroscience, social categorization, intergroup contact, race, ethnicity, diversity, and more.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Data Analysis in Psychology
courses.description:
Discussion of statistical analysis of psychological data - random samples, graphical and numerical techniques of descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, probability, sampling distribution, and hypothesis testing.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H; and Stat 1350.xx, 1450.xx, Math 1120, 1130, 1148, 1149, 1150, or 1151, or equiv, or Math Placement Level M or higher.
courses.prereq: 1100 or 1100H; and Stat 1350.xx, 1450.xx, Math 1120, 1130, 1148, 1149, 1150, or 1151, or equiv, or Math Placement Level M or higher

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description:
An overview of issues, methods, and techniques of scientific psychological research. Students must be pursuing majors or minors in Psychology.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Extraordinary Beliefs
courses.description: Considers beliefs in extraordinary phenomena through the application of the findings and principles of psychological science. Prereq: Not open to students with credit for 301.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for 301

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Positive Psychology
courses.description: Introduction to the field of positive psychology. Topics include positive affect, subjective well-being, optimism, psychological strengths, emotional intelligence, compassion, humor, and spirituality.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Motivation
courses.description: In this course we will survey (while reflecting on everyday applications) the integral role that motivation and related concepts, such as drive, need, affect, and emotion, play within Psychological Science to understand human behavior and identity formation.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.description: Overview of the psychology of human sexuality including the nature and variety of human sexual experience, theories and therapies regarding sexual issues. Prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H). Not open to students with credit for 333.02.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Interpersonal Relationships
courses.description: Surveys the scientific literature on interpersonal relationships, including family, friends, and romantic partnerships.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology Applied to Sport
courses.description: Psychological factors that influence sport participation and performance; psychological techniques to enhance performance; psychological problems associated with sport.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Creativity
courses.description: A critical examination of conceptual, theoretical, and methodological problems related to the systematic study of creativity; special attention to background factors related to creative behavior. Prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H). Not open to students with credit for 462 or 662.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
courses.description:
Examination of how observers perceive their environment through sensory information; emphasis on major sensory systems including vision, audition, spatial orientation, touch, taste, and olfaction.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
courses.description: Examination of how observers perceive their environment through sensory information; with an emphasis on vision and audition. Prereq: Honors standing, and 1100, 1100H, or 1100E. Not open to students with credit for 3310 (310).
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 1100, 1100H, or 1100E

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Memory and Cognition
courses.description:
An introduction to experimental study of human memory and cognition.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description:
Introduction to the structure and function of the nervous system in relation to behavior.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to the structure and function of the nervous system in relation to behavior. Prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H). Not open to students with credit for 3313 (313).
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H)

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Quantitative and Statistical Methods in Psychology
courses.description: A concentrated examination of applications of statistical tools in inference in contemporary psychology; hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, and analysis of variance. Prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H), and a grade of B or above in 2220 (220) or 2220H (220H). Not open to students with credit for 321 or 321H.
courses.prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H), and a grade of B or above in 2220 (220) or 2220H (220H)

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Social Psychology
courses.description:
An introduction to research in social psychology; topics include individual motivation, group behavior, attitudes, and perception of self and others.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H. Not open to students with credit for 2367.01 or 3325H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Social Psychology
courses.description: An in-depth, empirically based introduction to research in social psychology; topics include individual motivation, group behavior, attitudes, and perception of self and others. Prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H); or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 2367.01 (367.01), 3325 (325), or 325H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology
courses.description:
Examination of current theories and empirical findings regarding the major forms of psychopathology and treatment.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H. Not open to students with credit for 2367.02, 3331H, or 3331E.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology
courses.description: Examination of current theories and empirical findings regarding the major forms of psychopathology. Prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H); or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 2367.02, 3331 (331), 3331E (331E), or 331H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Adjustment
courses.description: Examination of psychological concepts and theories related to individual adjustment and adaptation. Prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H). Not open to students with credit for 335.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Life Span Developmental Psychology
courses.description:
Consideration of theories and research on psychological development across the lifespan; includes consideration of social policies that influence developmental outcomes.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Language and the Mind
courses.description:
Introduction to psychological processes for producing and understanding speech, the means by which these processes arise in the child, and their bases in the brain.
Prereq: 1100, Ling 2000, or 5000. Not open to students with credit for 3371H, Ling 3701, or 3701H. Cross-listed in Ling 3701.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Language and the Mind
courses.description:
Introduction to psychological processes for producing and understanding speech, the means by which these processes arise in the child, and their bases in the brain.
Prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100), 1100H (100H), Ling 2000 (Linguist 201), 2000H (200H), or 4000 (601); or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 3371 (371), 371H, Ling 3701 (Linguist 371), or 3701H (371H). Cross-listed in Ling 3701H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100), 1100H (100H), Ling 2000 (Linguist 201), 2000H (200H), or 4000 (601); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Stereotyping and Prejudice
courses.description:
Lectures address experimental research in stereotyping and prejudice; readings focus on historical, cultural, and sociological perspectives on issues related to gender, ethnicity, and social class.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description:
Examination of the neuroscientific approach to the study of cognition; primary focus on the psychobiology of memory, attention, language, and spatial orientation.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Organizational Psychology
courses.description:
Overview of theory, method, and practice of organizational psychology: motivation, job attitudes, leadership, groups, organizational design.
Prereq: 1100. Not open to students with credit for 4522.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Theories of Personality
courses.description: Major theoretical and research orientations in the study of normal and abnormal personality development, with a focus on personality processes. Prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H). Not open to students with credit for 530.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Childhood
courses.description: Introduction to the major phenomena, methods, theories, and findings of developmental psychology, especially as they apply to infancy and childhood. Prereq: 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H). Not open to students with credit for 550 or 550H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Childhood
courses.description: Introduction to the major phenomena, methods, theories, and findings of developmental psychology, especially as they apply to infancy and childhood. Prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H); or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 550 or 550H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 1100 (100) or 1100H (100H); or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Adolescence
courses.description:
An examination of the biological, psychological, and social aspects of normal adolescent development.
Prereq: 1100 or 1100H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: A Practical Guide to Ruling the World
courses.description:
Contemporary and historical research research as applied to governing and the governed, including social and political psychology, behavioral economics, and more. Reading and discourse on psychological research including: flags and symbols, authoritarianism, patriotism, protests and rebellion, taxation, the media, police psychology, conspiracy theories, and immigration.
Prereq: Completion of GE Foundation Social and Behavioral Sciences course.
courses.prereq: Completion of GE Foundation Social and Behavioral Sciences course

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Psychopharmacology
courses.description:
Introduction to the effects of drugs upon brain function.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major. Not open to students with credit for 3305, 305, or 597.01.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Science of Moral Understanding
courses.description:
We all struggle to understand those with different moral beliefs. This course examines difficult moral disagreements (e.g., abortion, euthanasia), using social psychology to reveal the basis of our moral judgments, the drivers of moral divides, and how to bridge them. We'll cover theory and practice, and develop skills for constructive dialogue and civil disagreement.
Prereq: 3325, 3325E or 3325H.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: The Self
courses.description:
Survey of classic and contemporary theory and research on social psychological study of the self; diverse approaches, and various gender, ethnic, and cross-cultural perspectives.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 2367 prior to SU13, 2367.01, 3325, 3325H, or 3375. Not open to students with credit for 475.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 2367 prior to SU13, 2367.01, 3325, 3325H, or 3375

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology and the Law
courses.description:
Contributions of psychological theories to the legal system and the role of mental health professionals in this system.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300. Not open to students with credit for 485.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Advanced Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description:
Advanced discussion of contemporary issues in behavioral neuroscience, including: synaptic pharmacology, drugs, and behavior, neurodegenerative diseases and the biological bases of psychopathology.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300, and a grade of B or above in 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300, and a grade of B or above in 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Judgment and Decision-Making
courses.description:
An overview of current models and empirical research on cognitive processes in human decision-making and judgment under risk or uncertainty.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300. Not open to students with credit for 508 or 4508H (508H).
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology Laboratory
courses.description:
Training in experimental and quantitative methods in cognitive psychology; laboratory experiments include topics such as memory, perception, and attention.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300; and a grade of C- or above in 3302, 3310, or 3312; and enrollment in Psych major. Not open to students with credit for 4520.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300; and a grade of C- or above in 3302, 3310, or 3312; and enrollment in Psych major

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Emotion
courses.description:
An examination of emotion focusing on how emotions are interconnected to other basic psychological processes such as cognition, motivation, decision making, and well-being.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Social Psychology Laboratory
courses.description:
Training in experimental and quantitative methods in social psychology. Experiments include topics such as attitudes, persuasion, social cognition, and group processes.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 2367 prior to SU13, 2367.01, 3325, 3325H, or 3375, and enrollment in Psych major. Not open to students with credit for 4510.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 2367 prior to SU13, 2367.01, 3325, 3325H, or 3375, and enrollment in Psych major

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Personal Security: Global and Local Perspectives
courses.description: Surveys the diverse psychological literature on personal security, a key ingredient in psychological well-being. Prereq: 1100. Not open to students with credit for 525.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description:
Introduction to health psychology; health-promoting and health-damaging behaviors; modification of health behaviors; stress and coping; management of illness; stress management strategies.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300. Not open to students with credit for 531.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Clinical Psychological Science
courses.description:
Surveys the scientific foundations of clinical psychological interventions and assessment techniques and considers their implications for the profession of clinical psychology.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300; and a grade of C- or above in 2367.02 or 3331.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300; and a grade of C- or above in 2367.02 or 3331

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Counseling Psychology
courses.description:
Issues within the field of counseling psychology including assessment, counseling skills, multicultural issues, career, professional, and ethical issues.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300; and a grade of C- or above in 2367.02, 3331, 3335, or 3530.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300; and a grade of C- or above in 2367.02, 3331, 3335, or 3530

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
courses.description:
Introduction to cross-cultural theories and research in various specialties in psychology (e.g., social, developmental, and counseling psychology).
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychology of Adult Years
courses.description:
Theory and research related to adulthood as a sequence of psychological stages involving adjustment and coping behaviors; relationship of adulthood to other life-span stages.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Language Development
courses.description:
A survey of children's language acquisition, including phonemes, words, morphology, and syntax. Roles for universal grammar, linguistic input, social interaction, and statistical learning are considered.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300. Not open to students with credit for 4554S.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Adolescent Sexuality
courses.description:
An examination of the psychological, biological, and social influences on adolescent sexuality.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220 and 2300

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Attitudes and Persuasion
courses.description:
Overview of the major psychological theories and research in the area of attitudes and persuasion - how people's opinions, beliefs, and evaluations are formed and modified.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 2367 prior to SU13, 2367.01, 3325, 3325H, or 3375. Not open to students with credit for 630.
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 2367 prior to SU13, 2367.01, 3325, 3325H, or 3375

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Hormones and Behavior
courses.description:
Exploration of the interactions among hormones, brain, and behavior through an integrative approach.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major. Not open to students with credit for 644 or Neurosc 5644 (644).
courses.prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Undergraduate Research in Psychology
courses.description: Supervised collaborative research in psychology. Prereq: Permission of instructor. Repeatable to a maximum of 15 cr hrs or 8 completions. This course is graded S/U.
courses.prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.description: Seminar designed to support the writing of the Thesis proposal and data collection, including proposal structure, literature review, research ethics, the IRB process, and data collection methodology. Prereq: Enrollment in Psych, and candidate for degree with research distinction, and permission of department.
courses.prereq: Enrollment in Psych, and candidate for degree with research distinction, and permission of department

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research I
courses.description: Seminar designed to support the writing of the Honors thesis proposal and data collection, including proposal structure, literature review, research ethics, the IRB process, and data collection methodology.  Prereq: Honors standing, and enrollment in Psych major, and candidate for degree with research distinction, and permission of department. Not open to students with credit for 783.01H or 783.02H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and enrollment in Psych major, and candidate for degree with research distinction, and permission of department

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Thesis Research II
courses.description: Seminar designed to support data collection/analysis, and writing and defending of the Thesis, including quantitative methods, data interpretation, summary, and presentation, writing results and discussion, poster presentation, and oral defense. Prereq: 4999.01.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research II
courses.description: Seminar designed to support data collection/analysis, and writing and defending of the Honors thesis, including quantitative methods, data interpretation, summary, presentation, writing results & discussion, poster presentation, and oral defense. Prereq: Honors standing, and 4999.01H; or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 783.02H or 783.03H.
courses.prereq: Honors standing, and 4999.01H; or permission of instructor

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Psychobiology of Learning & Memory
courses.description:
Integrate coverage of animal learning and human memory, focusing on three key components of the field: behavioral processes, brain systems, and clinical perspectives.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 3313; or a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major; or Grad standing.

courses.title: High-Level Vision
courses.description:
Examines the perceptual processes by which humans and other animals are able to obtain knowledge about the three-dimensional environment.
Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2220, 2300, and 3310; or a grade of C- or above in 3310, a grade of B or above in 3313 and Neurosc 3000, and Neuroscience major; or Grad standing.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Psychology
courses.description:
Survey of mathematical and computational modeling in psychology. Topics include psychophysical scaling, information processing, probabilistic choice, signal detection theory, model comparison, and Bayesian graphical modeling.

courses.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
courses.description: Cognitive science is an interdisciplinary study of the nature of human thought; psychological, philosophical, linguistic, and artificial intelligence approaches to knowledge representation. Prereq: A total of 12 cr hrs from any of the following areas: CSE, Ling, Philos, or Psych, or Grad standing, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 612, CSE 5531 (612), Ling 5612 (Linguist 612), or Philos 5830 (612). Cross-listed in CSE 5531, Ling 5612, and Philos 5830.

courses.subject: PSYCH
courses.title: Biological Psychiatry
courses.description:
Provides a contemporary overview of the biological bases of several significant psychopathologies, including mood disorders, schizophrenia, and PTSD/dissociative identity disorders.
Prereq: Honors standing; and a grade of C- or higher in Psych 2220 and Psych 2300, and Psych 3313 or Psych 3513; or a grade of B or above in Psych 3313 and Neurosc 3000 and Neuroscience major; or Grad standing.

courses.description:

courses.description:
Characterization, risk and protective factors, and treatment of delinquency with emphasis on current theories and research practices.

courses.description:
Team-taught seminar on selected topics from contemporary research areas in the field of behavioral neuroscience.

courses.subject: RELSTDS
courses.title: Literature and Religion
courses.description:
Study of relationships between religion and secular literature; analysis of religious and spiritual elements of literature and film of diverse cultures and historical periods.
Prereq: English 1110 (110) or equiv. Not open to students with credit for 2102.01H, CompStd 2102.01 (202.01), or 2102.01H (202.01H).

courses.subject: RELSTDS
courses.title: Comparative Sacred Texts
courses.description:
Introduction to religious views of the universe, the supernatural, social organization, ethics, etc., through sacred texts (oral and written) of diverse cultures and historical periods.
Prereq: English 1110.xx, or GE foundation writing and info literacy course, or equivalent. Not open to students with credit for CompStd 2102.02.

courses.subject: RELSTDS
courses.title: From Ishtar to Christ: The History of Mediterranean Religions
courses.description:
This course introduces students to the historical facts of 10 ancient Mediterranean religions in a context that trains them to study religions more generally. It also teaches them how two of the most prominent religions today--Judaism and Christianity--succeeded within a richly diverse religious marketplace, and how religions respond to their political, economic, and social environments.
Prereq: Not open to students with credit for Clas 2222. Cross-listed in Clas.
courses.prereq: Not open to students with credit for Clas 2222

courses.subject: RELSTDS
courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Religion
courses.description:
Introduction to the academic study of religion through comparison among major traditions (Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, etc.) and smaller communities.
Prereq: English 1110 or equiv. Not open to students with credit for 2370H or CompStd 2370H or 2370.
courses.prereq: English 1110 or equiv

courses.subject: RELSTDS
courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Religion
courses.description:
